title: Classification plan
description: The decisions an agent makes for one dataset. Execution belongs to driver.py, so this file carries choices from fixed menus and the prose that justifies them - never code. scripts/plan.py is what actually enforces the contract; this file exists so an editor can complete the fields and so tests/test_plan.py can pin the two together. If they ever disagree, plan.py is right.

schema_version.description: Bumped when the contract changes in a way that breaks an old plan.

dataset.description: Path to the labelled training file.

test_dataset.description: A separate labelled test file, held out untouched. Null splits a test set off `dataset` instead, using validation.test_size.

seed.description: One seed for every split and every model. Fixed configuration, never tuned.

reason.description: Which evidence decided it - the cardinality, the name convention, or the user's answer.

drop_columns.description: Entity keys, timestamps and identifier-like columns to exclude from the features - or [] when nothing is excluded. May not contain the target.

drop_rows_with_missing_label.description: A missing label cannot be imputed and cannot be scored, so this is an explicit answer rather than a default.

factor.description: IQR multiplier. Required when method is 'iqr'.

columns.description: Which numeric columns the rule applies to. Omit for all of them.

outlier_policy.description: Keep every row, or filter on an IQR fence.

cleaning.description: Step 3. Bounded on purpose: every action is from a menu the driver can execute. A free-form expression here would reopen the hole this design closes.

models.description: Step 4 and Step 5. Exactly two, and they must be different families - two of one family differ only in hyperparameters, so the comparison says nothing about inductive bias.

scale.description: Per model, not global: whether this family needs scaled inputs is a property of the estimator, and the report is graded on the difference.

scale_reason.description: Why this value. The registry states a strength of preference - 'not required', 'generally recommended', 'effectively required' - and the report is graded on telling those apart, so a bare boolean is not enough.

stopping.description: The report's 'Stopping criterion' cell: max_iter/tol and whether the cap was reached; the tree-growth limit; early stopping and what it monitored; or 'none - no iterative fit'. Never invent one you did not set.

overfitting_control.description: The report's 'Overfitting control' cell: max_depth, min_samples_leaf, pruning, or the regularisation that limits capacity. Name the mechanism actually in force, including the default you left alone.

grid.description: Hyperparameter name -> the values to try. Keys are bare parameter names, checked against this family's own get_params(); driver.py adds the `clf__` prefix that build_pipeline requires.

strategy.description: Must match `unit`: row -> holdout|stratified_kfold, entity -> grouped_holdout|stratified_group_kfold, time -> temporal. The wrong pairing is silent.

test_size.description: Fraction held out as the test set when no test_dataset is given.

val_fraction.description: Fraction of the remaining pool used to validate. A lever, not a constant.

n_splits.description: Required by the fold strategies, and capped by fold_cap(). Null for holdouts.

gap.description: Required by 'temporal': rows skipped between train and test. Null otherwise.

group_column.description: Required by the group strategies; the driver excludes it from the feature set automatically. Null otherwise.

metric.description: What the search optimises. Deliberately a narrower menu than primary_metric.name, because the scorer implements only these two - so the plan carries both fields and the reason explains any divergence.

final_fit_reason.description: Why that scope. 'pool' in particular means the test estimate is no longer untouched by selection, which the report has to say.

reason.description: The four inputs that decided it: the task objective, the class distribution, the cost of each error type, and whether the validation design can estimate it stably.

rejected.description: The metric you did not lead with. Must differ from `name` - rejecting the metric you chose reads as a decision that was never made.

model_version.description: The exact identifier you are being served as. Never copy an example; if you cannot determine it, ask.

harness.description: API, ChatUI, or 'Agent Harness such as <name> <version>'.

repository.description: The GitHub link to this skill, as given by the user.

report.description: Step 8 - the identity block drawn as the report header.

candidate_models.description: Every family considered with the number that put it in the running, each rejection and the number that killed it, and why the two survivors differ in inductive bias.

feature_engineering.description: Encoding, scaling, derived features, dropped columns - one line of rationale each, or why nothing was needed.

cleaning_why.description: The report's cleaning table, one row per issue.

validation_argument.description: Chosen because ... - the structure evidence that fixed the unit, then the arithmetic: rare rows per estimate, and what one flipped row moves.

performance_comparison.description: The gap between the two models, the spread, and what the gap is worth against the spread.

limitations.description: Bias-variance reading, any violated assumption, and what you would change.

narrative.description: The report's argument. Spliced in verbatim, so the report can never disagree with the run that produced it.
